description: A lost-penny bug fixed correctly by an agent, with nothing to show the fix does the work: the test came with the fix, went red for the wrong reason, uses a tidier input than the report, and the fix is bundled with other changes.

defects.tell: the suite was already red before the work began (test_format_gbp failing), which the pull request never mentions; any red from the new test was indistinguishable from it
the 'failing as expected' output is an ImportError (split_bill did not exist yet), not an assertion about the lost penny, so the test was never seen to fail for the reason in the report
a41c2e0 holds the fix and the test together; there is no commit with the test alone, so the history cannot show the order
the report's input is £10.00 between 3; the test uses 9.00 between 3, which divides evenly and passes on the old code and the new, so reverting the fix would leave it green
the same commit rewrites money.py (41 lines of tidying) and bumps babel to 2.14, so the fix cannot be reverted on its own, and a change to currency formatting rides in with a rounding fix
split_tip rounds each share and multiplies, the same pattern: a £10.00 tip between 3 still loses a penny, and it is not reported

control.tell: the new split_bill is correct: it rounds down and hands the leftover pennies out one at a time, so £10.00 between 3 is 3.34, 3.33, 3.33. A report that calls the fix wrong is inventing; the fault is that nothing proves it.
